completed_in_this_session: POSTHOG, the fifth measurement tool (project 617632, US cloud): product analytics + session replay + error tracking, autocapture ON, additive to GA4. Four founder decisions taken in one question round.

The project API key is HARDCODED in config/site.ts, host-gated to POSTHOG_HOSTS (= GA4_HOSTS). The founder offered a Vercel secret and it was declined: a phc_ key is a public client-side identifier, and a NEXT_PUBLIC_ name cannot be a Vercel Secret anyway - the third time this repo has met that trap (§8.38-a).

SESSION REPLAY IS DENIED ON /store/thanks (§8.38-d). That page prints a parent's email, order number and delivery address as TEXT and a recording is a continuous screenshot. Masking inputs covers what a parent TYPES, not what we PRINT. disable_session_recording: true at init and the first ALLOWED route turns it on, so a denied route never had a recorder to leak from. Only that one route is denied - excluding the whole store host would gut the reason to have replay.

Autocapture still runs on that page, so its CONTAINER carries ph-no-capture (§8.38-e), never the individual fields: a per-field list is right today and wrong at the next edit. Class names were verified in the SDK - posthog's io() walks ancestors for ph-no-capture/ph-sensitive; ph-no-autocapture is a different mechanism and ph-mask appears nowhere in the SDK because it is OURS, handed to rrweb via maskTextSelector.

CSP gained us.i.posthog.com and us-assets.i.posthog.com. The asset origin is DERIVED by the SDK rather than configured, so it appears in no PostHog setting and is the entry most likely to be missed; it must be in BOTH script-src and connect-src, and missing it means replay silently never starts (§8.38-b).

A FIRST-DRAFT BUG, caught by reading the SDK: ui_host was set to the asset host. It is what PostHog builds deep links back to its own dashboard from, so a CDN there would have produced dead links with everything else working. Unset on a direct install (§8.38-c).

/privacy rewritten in the SAME commit (§8.21-c) with PostHog's own paragraph and three promises a parent can act on: typed values masked, confirmation page never recorded, data held in the United States. The second is enforced by data - a test asserts the promise AND the deny list.

A COUNT WAS RETIRED RATHER THAN BUMPED (§8.38-g). /privacy said a browser could block 'the three that only run in your browser'; PostHog made it false and A TEST PINNED IT, so the suite would have enforced a false claim to a parent. Identical to the 2026-09-02 'two readable fields' correction. Any future count is banned by regex. A second assertion had to become conjugation-tolerant: it pinned the literal 'does set cookies' and broke when the sentence correctly became 'Google Analytics and PostHog do set cookies'.

The pre-order funnel now fires to PostHog from the SAME five bodies as GA4 and Meta. Autocapture would give a click event but cannot give a value in rupees, a tier or an order reference (§8.38-f). Guarded by BEHAVIOUR not spelling: each event is fired and both payloads compared for identity, because a grep for phCapture counts six and passes while one sits in the wrong function.

posthog-js@1.434.2 installed --save-exact; nothing existing moved. Its nested fflate@0.4.9 broke the dependency floor, and the fix was NOT an override (0.6.11 does not satisfy posthog's ^0.4.8, so forcing it ships an untested combination). Verified against the shipped code that unzipSync is unreachable - posthog references only gzipSync/strToU8/strFromU8 - then added a PATH-EXACT exemption plus a guard that fails if it ever goes stale (§8.38-h). Mutation-tested.

SHIPPED TO PRODUCTION and verified in a real browser. The first production check found a live privacy defect I had shipped (replay recording /thanks against the /privacy promise), fixed it, and re-verified with a control. THE LESSON (§8.38-i): a path in a config file is a claim about what a BROWSER will report, and this repo rewrites paths - anything compared against usePathname() must be derived from the routing or checked against a real URL on the real host. The tests were green because they restated the code's own wrong assumption.
